blocks.text: Organizing your workflow with smart mailboxes

Legal transcriptionists often handle dozens of active cases simultaneously. Keeping these organized in your inbox is vital. Instead of manually moving every email, create smart mailboxes. Go to Mailbox > New Smart Mailbox. You can set criteria based on the sender or specific keywords in the subject line. For example, create a mailbox that automatically collects all emails containing a specific case number.
Handling large audio files in Apple Mail

Sending and receiving large audio files is a standard part of your day. Apple Mail includes Mail Drop, which handles files up to 5 GB. When you attach a file that exceeds your provider's limit, Mail automatically uploads it to iCloud and sends a link instead. This prevents bounce-back errors that delay your work. Always check your attachment size before sending to ensure it triggers the Mail Drop feature.
Speeding up correspondence with keyboard shortcuts

Memorizing these shortcuts saves significant time over the course of a week. If you need to jump between mailboxes, use Command + 1 through Command + 9. These correspond to the order of your mailboxes in the sidebar. Setting up your favorite folders at the top of the sidebar makes this navigation much faster.

Transcriptionists must adhere to strict confidentiality standards. Ensure your Apple Mail settings are configured for security. Go to Mail > Settings > Accounts > Server Settings. Verify that your incoming and outgoing server connections use SSL or TLS. If you use a VPN for firm security, ensure it does not interfere with your mail connection. If you experience sync issues, try rebuilding your mailbox by selecting the mailbox in the sidebar and choosing Mailbox > Rebuild.

faq.question: Can I use Apple Mail for sensitive legal documents?
faq.answer: Yes, provided you follow your firm's security protocols, including using encrypted connections and ensuring your Mac is password-protected.

faq.question: How do I deal with emails not syncing?
faq.answer: Check your network connection first. If that fails, go to Mailbox > Rebuild to refresh the local database of your messages.

faq.question: What is the limit for attachments in Apple Mail?
faq.answer: Standard iCloud limits are 20 MB, but Mail Drop allows you to send files up to 5 GB by creating an expiring download link.
